step: Exercise Files image through reserved identity manager
logSnapshotBoundary: Downloaded job log after native test completion while development disk artifact upload remained in progress; not a claim that the whole job completed.
environment: Disposable Ubuntu 24.04 native KVM/libvirt CI; reserved identities and temporary fixture-owned image, channel and volume paths
qualifiedScope: Actual unsigned development Files guest uses the production Linux backend, reserved identity Manager and socket provenance checks.
After first cooperative guest shutdown, a SQLite trigger rejects the original runtime operation completion write; the runtime remains journaled as shutting-down.
After removing the trigger, production supervisor audit observes domain exit and completes the original owner/revision/deadline-bound shutdown journal.
Replaying the original shutdown operation returns stopped without another guest launch.
The fixture restarts the same instance and reuses its transfer process; actual unprivileged transfer round trips and foreign-role refusals pass before and after recovery.
The surrounding fixture completes its 1 GiB object round trip, reconnect/replay, disk-full refusal and retained-object verification across the two launches.
limitations: Injected database completion failure, not physical power loss or a real dropped network packet.
Direct Manager fixture with temporary qualified root paths, not installed controller/gateway/systemd confinement or HTTPS/passkey UI.
Controller/supervisor journal convergence is separately covered by a simulated-runtime integration test, not combined with this actual guest fixture.
Unsigned development image and ephemeral fixture catalog signing do not qualify a trusted release.
Physical guest filesystem consistency, production disk lifecycle, backup, cross-VM isolation, performance and release qualification remain unverified.
Overall workflow and artifact retention were still in progress when the log snapshot was captured.
